title: How do you set up your repo before starting a new project?
author: Time_Cat_5212
selftext:
Curious to hear from other AI game devs how you structure and setup your GitHub repo before starting a fresh new project.  What specifically do you set up, and why?

I've been focusing more on this preparatory work as I've seen amazing benefits to the quality of code and follow through with coding agents within a good structure.

Insight from others, especially those taking small projects from 0 to production, would be super helpful!

comments.author: Nessuno256
comments.body:
Pretty much the same as it was 10 years ago.

I import all the necessary packages, set up dependency injection, configure the boot loader, etc. Only now it’s much more automated. Plus to these, there are my local skills, a lot of documentation that I usually kept in my head, and so on.

replies.author: 3tt07kjt
replies.body: Boot loader? When I think of boot loaders I think of the code that loads the kernel, but maybe you mean something different.

replies.author: Nessuno256
replies.body: I'm referring to the mechanism that loads the resources and initializes the game systems. It is traditionally called “boot”

replies.author: 3tt07kjt
replies.body: Maybe. This is the first time I remember seeing it called that.

comments.author: Affectionate_Fact854
comments.body:
I personally set up the git repo and make it private 
Then I simply give ai the https link to make the initial commit 

Honestly to lazy to manually do bash now a days

comments.author: algorys
comments.body:
A "docs" folder containing Markdown files: design, ideas, etc.
An `agents.md` file.

Then, I list all the ideas regarding the project—somewhat haphazardly—and try to organize them.

replies.author: Baraga91
replies.body:
How much of this could you just let Claude do?

For a private project, Claude basically walked me through the bare minimum of steps necessary of setting up a a repo and organizes it as we go.

replies.author: algorys
replies.body:
I create the files myself. I prefer it that way.

Then, I let the AI ​​review the files and start working on the design.

Actually, at the start, I mainly design the game, its core concepts, and the features I want. Then, I strip it down to the essentials to create an initial MVP.

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body: What do you put in your agents file?

replies.author: algorys
replies.body: I only use agents.md and readme.md, then inside point to doc folder and design files.

comments.author: johnesco
comments.body: I set up a repro with Git Hub Projects and have a custom SDLC protocol that not only tracks code in Git and Github, but tracks choices and intention if the work done. Some people prefer less structure especially when vibe coding but for me the ticketing of the workflow is as important to me as the code itself.

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body: Curious, why SDLC for this and what does that offers for intent tracking that Git alone can't?

replies.author: johnesco
replies.body: Tracking the code is part of it, but I have a custom SDLC flow to help track ideas, understand what's done, what depends on what, tracking bugs, documenting changes, measure what's been tested and much more. Git tracks what was done. I use the GH project to track and plan unfinished work.

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body: I'm interested in trying something similar.  Can you give an example of how it works?

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body: SDLC.  Never worked with that before

replies.author: johnesco
replies.body: SDLC is "software development life cycle". It can have different forms and styles. Waterfall, Agile, and others, it's just the process with which you go from idea, to code, to shipped feature. Most people like to skip it all and just code, but this method brings a control and planning that helps AI not go off track so much. The way you choose to do it may be very different. I do it as a way to show all design choices being made.

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body: Oh. Lmao. I googled it and got "synchronous data link" XD
